result:
`bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` is green (11 tests, 0 failures), including the 9 new ones.

I made the post excerpt optional and auto-derived. `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts` now declares `excerpt` as `z.string().trim().max(500).optional()`, so a missing, empty, or whitespace-only value passes validation while blank titles and bodies are still rejected with 422. A new `app/Support/excerpt.ts` holds `deriveExcerpt(body)` — trims the body, returns it whole at ≤140 characters, otherwise keeps the first 140 characters but backs up to the last whitespace when the boundary would split a word (leaving 140 intact when character 141 is whitespace, and cutting flat at 140 for an unbroken run), then right-trims and appends a single `…` — plus `resolveExcerpt(payload)`, which prefers the submitted excerpt and falls back to the derived one. `PostController.store()` and `PostController.update()` both route the excerpt through `resolveExcerpt`, so an update that clears the field re-derives from the new body. `resources/js/pages/posts/New.tsx` and `Edit.tsx` label the field "Excerpt (optional)" with a placeholder explaining the fallback and pin the form's excerpt to a `string` (the wire type is now optional) so the input stays controlled; `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` and `pages.gen.ts` were regenerated with `bunx guren codegen`. Tests live in `tests/PostExcerpt.test.ts`, covering both worked examples from the request character-for-character alongside create/update round-trips through the HTTP layer.
